title: Innovation advantage depends on connected capability ecosystems, while most economies leave substantial scientific and technological potential unused
source_unit: World Intellectual Property Organization, Innovation Capabilities Outlook 2026
geography: 193-country global innovation ecosystem comparison across science, technology, entrepreneurship, and production capabilities, using data spanning 2001-2023

denominator.unit: countries and economies analyzed in the Innovation Capabilities Outlook

capabilities_mapped.unit: innovation capabilities mapped across science, technology, entrepreneurship, and production

data_dimensions.unit: capability dimensions: science, technology, entrepreneurship, and production

data_sources.value: patents, trademarks, scientific publications, and exports

ecosystem_mechanism.value: innovation emergence depends on connections among capabilities rather than isolated strengths

observations.method: WIPO and Harvard Growth Lab capability-network analysis using cross-country indicators from patents, trademarks, publications, and exports over 2001-2023.
observations.uncertainty: Capability indicators measure observable outputs and networks, not every informal, public-sector, subsistence, or locally embedded innovation activity; cross-country comparability depends on source coverage.
observations.subgroup: Researchers, firms, entrepreneurs, production workers, universities, governments, investors, and regions building or translating knowledge into economic and social outputs.
observations.counterinterpretation: Connected capability profiles can support innovation, but they do not guarantee inclusive distribution, good jobs, public value, or successful implementation of every technology.

denominator.unit: economies analyzed in the global innovation-capability comparison

technological_potential_fulfillment.unit: percent of countries reported as fulfilling their technological potential

technology_underuse.unit: percent potential annual increase in technologies from better leveraging existing capabilities

entrepreneurial_underuse.unit: percent potential annual increase in entrepreneurial innovations from better leveraging existing capabilities

scientific_underuse.unit: percent potential annual increase in scientific discoveries from better leveraging existing capabilities

observations.method: WIPO capability-network estimates of unrealized output associated with stronger connections and more effective use of existing national capability portfolios.
observations.uncertainty: Potential gains are model-based counterfactual estimates, not guaranteed output increases; they depend on institutions, finance, skills, demand, governance, and implementation.
observations.subgroup: Economies with fragmented innovation systems, firms and researchers facing translation gaps, entrepreneurs, public funders, and workers affected by technological development pathways.
observations.counterinterpretation: Capability underuse may reflect deliberate specialization, measurement limits, market size, political choices, or constraints that cannot be removed by connection alone.

observations.period: 2026; diversification, complexity, and regional innovation pathways

denominator.unit: global innovation ecosystems analyzed by WIPO

not_meaningfully_diversified.unit: percent of ecosystems reported as not meaningfully diversified

complexity_gains_elusive.unit: percent of economies for which complexity gains remain elusive

asia_pathway.value: China, India, and Viet Nam are described as using smart diversification and capability management strategies

regional_mismatch.value: Europe has strong foundations but translation challenges; Asia has balanced capabilities but commercialization challenges; Africa is advised to build foundations while gradually targeting complexity

observations.method: WIPO comparison of capability diversity, complexity, and connected innovation pathways across regional and national ecosystems.
observations.uncertainty: Regional descriptions summarize heterogeneous economies and should not be treated as universal regional characteristics or causal development prescriptions.
observations.subgroup: Countries at different development levels, regional innovation systems, universities, firms, entrepreneurs, workers, and policymakers choosing diversification strategies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Complexity and diversification are not the only measures of social value; resilience, public goods, cultural production, and local appropriateness may not rank highly on these metrics.

observations.period: 2026; complex capabilities, upgrading, and development options

denominator.unit: economies in the WIPO innovation-capability pathway analysis

technological_capability_rarity.unit: percent-plus of countries reported as developing the rarest and most demanding technological capabilities

annual_upgrading.unit: approximate percent of countries that upgrade toward rarer and more rewarding innovation fields each year

pathway_principle.value: strategic diversification from existing strengths is presented as more useful than copying universal solutions

implementation_boundary.value: innovation capability does not by itself establish distributional outcomes, employment quality, environmental effects, or public legitimacy

observations.method: WIPO capability complexity and relatedness analysis identifying accessible diversification pathways and rare capability development.
observations.uncertainty: Pathway opportunity estimates are strategic diagnostics rather than causal forecasts; upgrading depends on political economy, institutions, skills, finance, infrastructure, and external conditions.
observations.subgroup: Policymakers, firms, universities, technical workers, entrepreneurs, investors, regions seeking new capabilities, and communities affected by industrial transformation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Targeting complexity can increase concentration or lock in an elite innovation agenda if local needs, worker voice, environmental limits, and public accountability are not included.

related_sources.claim: WIPO's executive summary provides the capability, concentration, and strategic-pathway findings.
WIPO's innovation-capabilities program provides the navigator, datasets, and methodological context.

boundary: This record adds an innovation-ecosystem route across science, technology, entrepreneurship, production, complexity, diversification, regional development, and capability power. It uses aggregate WIPO and Harvard Growth Lab analysis, not respondent-level worker histories, firm case files, individual patent attribution, causal technology forecasts, or proof that capability concentration produces identical social outcomes everywhere.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official WIPO publication page, executive summary, and launch materials reviewed for the capability dimensions, 193-economy frame, 2,508 capabilities, potential output gains, concentration, diversification, complexity, regional pathways, and policy boundaries.
